name: Quad and hip flexor stretch
pattern: Static hold: the hip straightens behind you, often with the knee bent, lengthening the front of the hip and thigh.
setup: Kneel on a pad, one knee down under the hip, other foot forward, both knees about 90°.
Hands on the hips or the front knee, chest tall.
Tuck your tailbone under: tilt the pelvis back before you move.

steps.text: Keep the pelvis tucked, squeeze the back glute and shift the hips slightly forward.
Stay still 15-30 s. Feel it at the front of the back hip; ribs stay down.
Come out slowly, then switch sides.

cues.cue: Tuck the tailbone and squeeze the back glute before you lean in.
cues.why: A posterior pelvic tilt reduced hip flexor resistance; the plain lunge stretch did not.

cues.cue: Ribs down, chest tall; do not arch the low back.
cues.why: Arching lets the low back bend instead of the hip.

cues.cue: For the quad, bring the heel to the glute with the knees side by side.
cues.why: Knee out to the side lets the hip bend and slackens the front of the thigh.

cues.cue: Ease in to a mild pull, never pain.
cues.why: Gentle stretches still gain range; stretching into pain did not help and can irritate the muscle.

cues.cue: Hold 15-30 s, 2-4 times, about 60 s in total per side.
cues.why: 30 s holds gave the same gains as 60 s; aim for at least 5 min per muscle each week, most days.

cues.cue: Best after training. Before, keep it under 60 s per muscle and finish with a dynamic warm-up.
cues.why: Short holds cost almost no strength or power; long holds (60 s or more) do. Stretching does not speed recovery.

breathing: Breathe slowly and normally. Ease a little deeper as you breathe out.

tempo.note: Ease in for about 3 s, hold 15-30 s, ease out. Repeat 2-4 times each side.

mistakes.name: Arching the low back
mistakes.looks: You lunge forward and the belly pushes out, low back sways.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the pelvis, ribs down; move only a little forward.
mistakes.why: The low back bends instead of the hip, so the hip flexor barely stretches.

mistakes.name: Knee drifts out
mistakes.looks: In the standing quad stretch the bent knee swings out or forward.
mistakes.fix: Knees side by side, thigh pointing down.
mistakes.why: The quad goes slack at the hip.

mistakes.name: Bouncing
mistakes.looks: You bob in and out of the stretch instead of holding still.
mistakes.fix: Ease in slowly, then stay still and let it relax.
mistakes.why: Bouncing triggers the muscle to tighten back and can strain it.

mistakes.name: Holding your breath
mistakes.looks: You tense up: shoulders creep up, jaw tight, breath held.
mistakes.fix: Breathe slowly; let each breath out take you a little deeper.
mistakes.why: Tension fights the stretch; relaxed breathing lets the muscle let go.

safety: Knee pain on the floor: kneel on a folded mat or use the standing version.
Pull the heel gently; stop if the knee pinches.
Low back pain: keep the tuck and use a smaller range.

variants.change: Back shin up a wall or bench: knee bent much more, strong quad stretch; start upright and far from the wall.
Same-side arm reaches up and slightly away: adds the side of the trunk.
Contract-relax: push gently against the stretch for 3-6 s, relax, then ease deeper. Similar range gains to static holds; also best after training.
A partner moves the limb. Go slowly and say when you feel a mild pull; the partner holds there, never pushes into pain.
Moving version: controlled swings through the range, 8-12 reps. Better before training than long holds.

subtypes.name: Couch stretch
subtypes.change: Back knee near a wall or bench, shin up it; front foot forward. Stay upright and tucked.

subtypes.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
subtypes.change: One knee down, other foot forward. Tuck the pelvis and shift a little forward.

subtypes.name: Standing hip flexor stretch
subtypes.match: standing hip flexor|supported one leg standing hip flexor
subtypes.change: Long split stance, back heel up, back knee straight; tuck the pelvis and press the hips forward.

subtypes.name: Standing quad stretch
subtypes.change: Stand on one leg, hold a support; pull the heel to the glute, knees together.

subtypes.name: Edge-of-bench hip flexor stretch
subtypes.change: On your back at the edge of a bench or bed, hug one knee; let the other leg hang down.

subtypes.name: Lying quad stretch
subtypes.change: Face down or on your side, pull one heel toward the glute, knees together.

subtypes.name: Kneeling lean-back quad stretch
subtypes.change: Kneel and sit on your heels, hands behind you; lean back slowly, hips pushing up.

metrics.label: Movement during hold
metrics.good: < 3° once you are in the stretch

motion.basis: Pelvic tuck from gonzalez2024; dose from garber2011, bandy1994, thomas2018. All joint angles are estimates from the usual stretch positions, not measured.
